newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Surgical steps up fight for Circon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Surgical steps up fight for Circon.

text.p: U.S. Surgical Corp, engaged in a bitter battle to acquire Circon Corp, said Monday it would try to elect two directors to Circon's board and open the company to a takeover.
U.S. Surgical said it had filed preliminary proxy solicitation materials with the Securities and Exchange Commission to elect two Circon directors.
It said it had also proposed a shareholder resolution urging Circon directors to arrange for the prompt sale of the company to the highest bidder.

"Although Circon shareholders have shown overwhelming support for a merger of the two companies, Circon's board and management have continually refused to meet with us," U.S. Surgical Chief Executive Leon Hirsch said in a press release. "The upcoming election of directors and the shareholder resolution will give Circon shareholders the opportunity to begin the process of taking control of the company."

U.S. Surgical proposed Charles Elson, a professor at Stetson University College of Law in St. Petersburg, Fla., and Victor Krulak, president of Words Ltd of San Diego, Calif., for the two Circon director positions up for election.
U.S. Surgical said earlier this month it had increased its stake in Circon to 14.9 percent through a tender for Circon shares at $14.50 each.
Circon earlier rejected a $17-a-share takeover offer from U.S. Surgical. Initially, U.S. Surgical bid $18 a share.
U.S. Surgical shares were down one point at 36 in morning trading. Circon was off 1/8 at 14-1/2.
